field: Original high quality game art for Époque des batailles, a stylized low-poly historical battle game. A single VERTICAL PORTRAIT contact sheet, 3:4 aspect ratio, containing TWO separate landscape screenshots of the SAME believable early nineteenth-century battlefield, stacked in two EXACTLY equal-height panels, separated by a hard straight cut at precisely the center with no border, gap or text. Each half must be usable as an immersive full-bleed game viewport. Deliberate fine faceted shapes, readable toy-soldier silhouettes, muted fabric, realistic scale of troops within the scene, high fidelity Unreal-style diffuse lighting, never photoreal or excessively detailed. The same field near Waterloo: a shallow ridge, an old stone farmhouse with a correct pitched tiled roof sitting ridge-up, a sunken lane with hedgerows, organized blue infantry and ruddy red infantry in separate formations, flags, light morning powder smoke without the field disappearing behind it. Landscape continues beyond the play area into Belgian farmland and woods, a plausible sloping horizon with no visible edge of terrain, no magical effects, no corpses or gore. Top panel: an oblique elevated tactical camera looking down across broad formations, a clear pale road and farmhouse as navigation landmarks, and the distant rolling terrain filling its upper third. Bottom panel: a third-person shoulder-level camera behind a blue Napoleonic company officer, small enough to see around him, in foreground lower center-left, dark blue coat and shako, friendly soldiers extending to left, open field and red formations in the middle distance, scene playable with unobstructed center and right sightline. No text, no letters or numerals, no logos, no interface, no icons, no dividing drawn line. Art direction A: crisp late morning sun from upper left, soft olive and sage vegetation with light limestone and soft slate blue uniforms, well-defined but soft-rimmed shadows along the ridge, warm cotton clouds in a muted cyan sky, distant farmland and ribbons of hedges. Readable tactical staging and evenly lit landscape. Clear breathable midtones.
